accepted.sentence: During a passage, the performer supports the fixed section with the left hand and guides the moving assembly with the right.
Moving the slide gradually between note positions can create a continuous pitch sweep, a characteristic gliding effect.
The tongue briefly interrupts the airstream at the mouthpiece to separate notes or shape crisp musical attacks.
Higher pitches generally require firmer, faster lip vibration, while lower pitches use a looser embouchure and slower vibration.
A mute placed inside the flared end changes the tone and often reduces volume, depending on its design.
Players take breaths between phrases, planning airflow so sustained notes and connected passages remain steady.
In orchestral music, it commonly supplies harmonic inner parts or reinforces low lines beneath brighter melodic instruments.
Because the moving assembly reaches well forward, performers need clear space in front of them while playing.
